rules.law_name: Hoboken Code Chapter 155, Article II, General Regulations
rules.title: Hoboken rent-control increase limits and surcharges
rules.requirement: For covered Hoboken rental housing, a landlord generally may raise rent at lease expiration or termination only by the lesser of 5% or the applicable CPI differential, and may not impose more than one such cost-of-living increase in any twelve-month period. Other increases or surcharges, including tax, water and sewer, capital-improvement, and hardship increases, are allowed only as authorized by the chapter and, where required, after approval and tenant notice.
rules.key_value: Regular increase: lesser of 5% or CPI differential; no more than one cost-of-living increase in any 12-month period; capital-improvement surcharge may not increase base rent by more than 33 1/3% in any 12-month period

coverage.other_unresolvable: The excerpt applies to 'housing space in dwellings to which this chapter is applicable' but does not include the chapter's coverage definitions; it also references exemptions for newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, without defining them in the excerpt.
coverage.summary: Applies to housing space in dwellings covered by Hoboken Chapter 155, but this excerpt does not state the full coverage criteria.

rules.exemptions: The excerpt references eligibility determinations for a newly constructed dwelling exemption and for a building completely vacant since January 1, 1984, but does not provide the exemption definitions.
rules.penalty: Any rent increase at a time other than lease expiration or termination of a periodic lease is void; any increase above that authorized by the chapter is void, and excess rents after October 1, 1985 must be refunded or credited to the tenant subject to the stated two-year limitation and repose provisions.
rules.interaction: Tax and water/sewer surcharges are not considered rent for purposes of computing cost-of-living rental increases; the disclosure statement must also acknowledge New Jersey's Truth-in-Renting Act.
rules.quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
